review_response.resolution: The alternating tensor explicitly spans V^{H0}; normality preserves this full one-dimensional space.
The proof defines the K-module W, its coordinate functions z_i and their product in C[W]^K, with values one at the tuple and zero at the origin.

review_response.resolution: Section 4 states -v is in Fp*, names the intermediate cubic field E and its separable inclusion, and uses Fp-linearity to cancel the scalar.

answers.what_is_new: The explicit invariant exceptional quotient pairs supply nonspherical finite-stabilizer cases for the general/disconnected classification. The text credits Long's earlier group and spherical results. Further recomposition and coefficient-algebra claims are identifiable; the reader cannot establish priority from the PDF alone.
answers.conceptual_reason: Weights and integration by parts force purity; a selected prime denominator and nonzero binary coefficient force marked nonvanishing. Klein identities and Cartier pullback compute that coefficient on a cubic. Structural reductions and finite-trace separation propagate the examples.
answers.hardest_step_and_location: Section 4's cubic/Cartier coefficient comparison, equations (4.5)-(4.6), with Appendices B-C; structural reductions in Section 6 and finite-trace separation in Lemma 7.1.
answers.limitations: Complex groups with reductive identity components and regular functions; exceptional marked nonvanishing at selected orders; representation-theoretic existence rather than coordinate bounds for general quotients; recomposition/ring statements concern the constructed polynomial subalgebra.
answers.verification_obstacles: The binary-to-affine coefficient bridge is now explicit. Remaining work is checking cited structural results, polynomial identities and the Section 8 valuation/descent argument; these are supplied proof obligations, with no definite missing central proof data identified by the reader.
